header:
Date: 2026-09-13
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AM), Marco (Redwood CSM), Devon (Redwood SE), Lina (Sienna Head of Platform), Marcus (Sienna ML), Ruth (Sienna IT Sec)
summary: Kickoff for onboarding Sienna Health onto Redwood. Covered goals (pilot NLU features, embeddings + retrieval, secure VPC deployment), basic timeline, security requirements (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), initial benchmark/POC planning, and next steps to share docs and schedule a deep technical benchmark session.
topics: Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC)
Security and compliance requirements (SSO, KMS, audit logs)
Pilot scope: embeddings + retrieval + chat for triage
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. Uh this is Aisha from Redwood, I'll run things quick, we've got Marco and Devon from our side.
[00:08] Lina Patel: Hi Aisha, thanks, excited to get started, we talked a bit over email but keen to map out timeline and what infra we need.
[00:15] Marco Ruiz: Quick intros, I'm Marco CSM, I'll be running onboarding and timeline. Devon is our solutions engineer who'll handle the SE parts.
[00:22] Devon Lee: Hi all, hi Lina, Marcus, Ruth. Happy to dig in, I'll cover network, VPC, and model selection.
[00:30] Marcus Chen: Hi, Marcus here. We're mostly focused on embeddings for semantic search and a lightweight generative assistant for triage. Latency is important but cost is also a big factor.
[00:40] Ruth Gomez: Ruth from security — we need details on encryption, audit logs, and SSO. We'll need SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration.
[00:47] Aisha Khan: Totally makes sense. For success criteria, what would you call a win for the pilot? Lina?
[00:52] Lina Patel: A win is reliable retrieval for 10k documents with sub-200ms lookup and a chat flow that handles 80% of triage intents without hallucination. Also stickiness — internal teams should adopt it within 4 weeks.
[01:05] Devon Lee: Okay that's helpful. So for architecture, two options: hosted Redwood API for fastest time-to-value, or Redwood Private (VPC). Given your security needs sounds like VPC/private is likely.
[01:18] Marcus Chen: We prefer private due to PHI concerns, but we want to understand overhead.
[01:24] Marco Ruiz: Yeah, private gives you customer-managed VPC with dedicated control plane and optional on-prem connector, we can scope that in the next steps.
[01:33] Ruth Gomez: For KMS — we use AWS KMS — can we integrate and have CMKs controlled by us?
[01:39] Devon Lee: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys for private deployments; we'll share the KMS integration doc. There's minor setup on our side for envelope encryption.
[01:47] Aisha Khan: On compliance, we have SOC 2 type II docs; I'll share the security pack after the call.
[01:54] Lina Patel: Great. On performance: Marcus, what's your 95th token latency goal per request?
[02:00] Marcus Chen: For retrieval then model inference combined, under 500ms 95th is ideal, but for the triage assistant under 1s might be okay to start.
[02:09] Devon Lee: That aligns with dedicated GPU pools — we can size for your expected qps. If we start with smaller capacity and ramp, we recommend a short benchmark where we run your prompts and dataset to figure the right config.
[02:21] Lina Patel: Sounds good. Timeline wise we want to launch an internal pilot in 6 weeks. Is that doable?
[02:28] Marco Ruiz: Six weeks is tight but doable for a VPC pilot — depends on approvals and access. Typical items: SSO generation, network peering, service account creation, sample data prep.
[02:39] Ruth Gomez: We'll need an IP allowlist and egress limits too.
[02:43] Devon Lee: We'll send the network and firewall checklist. For VPC peering we need a static egress IP and ports list; also if you prefer private link we have an option. Sometimes transcription notes — sorry — private link is, um, PrivateLink also supported.
[02:58] Marcus Chen: Regarding models, are you recommending smaller quantized models or larger ones? We need accuracy > 90% on intent classification.
[03:07] Devon Lee: For embeddings and retrieval we usually run open embeddings models — we can start with an optimized small-quant model for cost, then test a mid-size for quality. We'll provide model profiling recommendations.
[03:18] Aisha Khan: We'll also surface Redwood Optimize suggestions — batching and caching settings that usually reduce token cost.
[03:25] Lina Patel: Do you support fine-tuning or we'll do retrieval + RAG?
[03:29] Devon Lee: Both. For initial pilot we recommend RAG + vector search. Fine-tuning can come later once we see drift/regressions.
[03:36] Ruth Gomez: For audit logs, retention policy — can we retain detailed logs for 13 months?
[03:40] Marco Ruiz: Yes, our enterprise plans include configurable audit log retention — we'll confirm limits for your tier and any additional costs.
[03:48] Lina Patel: Good. Also SSO — we use Okta.
[03:51] Devon Lee: SSO via SAML Okta is supported, we'll share the SSO quickstart.
[03:55] Marcus Chen: About data residency, will the private deployment be in our AWS region? We're in us-east-1.
[03:59] Marco Ruiz: Yes we can pin region to us-east-1 for Private deployments and dedicated capacity.
[04:05] Aisha Khan: Next up, action items — we'll send the security pack, network checklist, and onboarding checklist. Then set the benchmark session for next week.
[04:12] Lina Patel: Sounds like plan. Also can you send a sample pilot plan and success metrics template?
[04:16] Marco Ruiz: Yes — will include KPIs: latency, accuracy, cost per 1k queries, adoption metrics.
[04:22] Marcus Chen: One more question — how do you handle fallback if model or nodes are down? We need graceful degradation.
[04:27] Devon Lee: We have smart routing and fallback policies: auto-fallback to compatible model variants or a lower-cost replica; plus retries with jitter. We'll document SLAs and failure modes.
[04:37] Ruth Gomez: We'll need to review the incident response plan and runbook.
[04:40] Marco Ruiz: Noted, we'll include runbook and escalation paths.
[04:44] Aisha Khan: Ok last quick note about pricing: we'll send estimated committed capacity pricing for Dedicated and a comparison for Hosted vs Private.
[04:53] Lina Patel: Thanks — that's helpful. One small thing — do you support encryption in transit with mTLS for private connections?
[04:58] Devon Lee: Yes mTLS is available for Private deployments; we'll include config steps.
[05:04] Aisha Khan: Great. We'll wrap there. Thanks everyone.
[05:07] Marco Ruiz: Thanks, Lina, Marcus, Ruth. We'll follow up with docs and calendar invite for the benchmark deep dive.
[05:13] Lina Patel: Thanks team, bye.
[05:15] (call ends)
